thesis: NVR (NYSE: NVR), homebuilder with land-light lot purchase agreements and a mortgage arm. Q3 2026 10-Q (filed 2026-11-04) read: balance sheet, income statement, cash flow, VIE note and MD&A order data. Q3 homebuilding revenue 2,349.3M (-8%), 9M 6,463.9M (-13%); Q3 NI 248.6M vs 342.7M (-27%), 9M NI 683.4M vs 976.0M; gross margin 18.3% vs 21.1%; new orders Q3 4,391 (-7%) but 9M +4%; backlog 10,121 units (+10%), 4,585M (+4%); cancellation rate 21.0% vs 19.4%; management says demand weakened further (affordability, rates, inventory). Close 5,468.04 (2026-11-20) x 2,645,788 shares (2026-10-31 cover) = 14.47B = 13.8x TTM NI 1,047.2M (1,339.8-976.0+683.4), 4.2x book 3,435M. TTM OCF 851.8M less capex 33.6M = FCF 818.2M (5.7%); inventory build 649M in 9M. Homebuilding cash 1,091M vs senior notes 908M. 9M buybacks 1,242.8M (about 1.8x 9M FCF of roughly 382M, funded from cash, which fell from 1,884M). Contract land deposits 1,073M gross with 156M allowance (impairments 55M in 9M).
counterthesis: Earnings and margins are falling (NI -27% in Q3, gross margin -280bp) in a rate and affordability squeeze, so TTM 13.8x flatters; 9M run-rate NI is about 911M annualised (own estimate, about 15.9x). Buybacks of 1.24B in 9M exceed 9M FCF and are shrinking the cash cushion and book value (equity 3.86B to 3.43B). Contract land deposits are 1.07B at risk with rising impairments. Cancellations rising. Quote is a Nov 20 close after a drop from 5,793 on 11-16, cause not read.
invalidation: Downgrade if orders turn negative on a sustained basis, gross margin falls below about 17%, deposit impairments accelerate, or buybacks continue to outrun FCF while cash falls. Upgrade case needs peers (PHM, DHI, LEN, TOL), through-cycle margin history, the 2026-10-22 release read, and verified quote origins.
